transcript.text: Alright, let's get this coordination meeting started. We've got tomorrow's inbound delivery — one palletized lot of generator housings and one lot of communications cable reels — and I need to publish final lane assignments before everyone leaves today. The draft plan currently shows all three staging lanes as interchangeable with no special receiving controls listed. Before I lock in assignments, I need to hear from each of you: warehouse ops NCO, movement control officer — are there any changes or issues affecting tomorrow's receiving plan that I need to factor in? Anything affecting Lane 1, Lane 2, or Lane 3 that would make one more suitable than another for either the generator housings or the cable reels?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Sir, there's a critical issue you need to factor in before locking in lane assignments. This morning I confirmed that only Lane 2 has a current floor-load certification for the 1,800-kilogram generator-housing pallet. The certification paperwork is filed in the warehouse binder, but it has not been added to the yard diagram yet — which is why the draft plan still shows all three lanes as interchangeable. The generator-housing pallet needs to go to Lane 2; Lane 1 or Lane 3 cannot be certified for that weight load.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Sir, I have a critical lane constraint to report. This afternoon I received the carrier's vehicle diagram and confirmed that the cable-reel tilt-bed requires a 4.0-meter turning clearance that is only available at Lane 3. This diagram has not yet been included in the movement-control brief, which is why the draft plan doesn't reflect it. The cable reels need to go to Lane 3 — neither Lane 1 nor Lane 2 can accommodate that turning clearance.
transcript.speaker: A3
